title: Give a record its own methods

blocks.text: A record body may hold instance methods, static methods (such as a factory), implementations of the interfaces the record declares, and overrides of the methods the record generates.
and the record `Person(String name, int age) implements Printable`. Write its four methods:

items: `boolean isAdult()`: `true` when the age is 18 or more;
`static Person createAdult(String name)`: a person of that name, aged 18;
`String toString()`: overridden to read `Person named <name> is <age> years old`.

blocks.text: Do not touch `equals` or `hashCode`: the generated ones must keep comparing the components.

new Person("Alice", 30).isAdult()     -> true
new Person("Tim", 17).isAdult()       -> false
Person.createAdult("Frank")           -> Person with name "Frank", age 18
new Person("Alice", 30).print()       -> "Person: Alice, 30 years old"
new Person("Bob", 25).toString()      -> "Person named Bob is 25 years old"

cases.says: isAdult, createAdult and print work for an ordinary adult.
A person of exactly 18 is an adult, and one of 17 is not.
toString is overridden to read 'Person named Bob is 25 years old'.
Overriding toString leaves equals and hashCode comparing the components.
Two people whose equal names are separate String objects, built at run time, are equal.

concepts: A record body may add instance methods of its own.
A record can implement an interface.
A generated method such as toString can be overridden, and the generated equals and hashCode still compare components.
